Title: SmilesPE: tokenizer algorithm for SMILES, DeepSMILES, and SELFIES
Description: Splits a SMILES string into substructure tokens with SMILES Pair Encoding, which learns its vocabulary from data instead of treating each character as a unit. Li and Fourches adapted byte-pair encoding from language modelling, merging the most frequent adjacent symbol pairs across 3.4 million ChEMBL SMILES until 3,002 recurring fragments, from functional groups to ring systems, became single tokens. Sequences come out shorter than atom-level ones and matched or beat them across 24 QSAR benchmarks. The bundled vocabulary is the ChEMBL one, and output is truncated or padded to 50 tokens.
Interpretation: Up to 50 substructure tokens from a ChEMBL-derived SMILES pair encoding vocabulary.
